change_summary: PLOS ONE has retracted this paper on phishing URL detection with an RNN-LSTM. The editors cite concerns about peer review integrity and possible manipulation of the publication process. They say these concerns call the validity and provenance of the results into question. The whole paper is affected, including its accuracy and F1 claims, so it should not be relied on or cited as support.
evaluation: Your draft cites Dutta [14] in Section 3 as "the main evidence" for choosing an LSTM, and in Section 4 as the source of the starting model settings. PLOS ONE retracted the whole paper and says the validity and provenance of its results are in question. Both uses are affected. Section 3 rests on the retracted accuracy and F1 claims and skipped a model-selection study because of them. Section 4 takes parameter values from the paper and plans to read your results against its published numbers. Since the paper is both key evidence and a source of methods, the impact is high.
recommendation: Raise this with your co-authors or supervisor, since both the LSTM choice (Section 3) and the starting settings (Section 4) rest on a paper PLOS ONE has retracted. Replace Dutta [14] with independent evidence, re-derive the settings, and drop the comparison with its published numbers.
